evidence_units.mechanism: Ordered BCC (B2) phase formation with no thermodynamic driving force or kinetic pathway for phase separation under these conditions, confirmed by absence of superlattice contrast from precipitates and homogeneous APT reconstruction.
evidence_spans: Samples of the AlCoFeNi alloy were isothermally annealed at either 600 ° C or 1000 ° C for 15 h.
The samples exhibited a polycrystalline microstructure consisting of large grains.
Based on these images the microstructure for both samples appears to be a single phase since no phase separation or second phase precipitation is evident from these SEM images.
The superlattice spots at {100} positions (one such spot is highlighted by a white circle and labeled as <010> in Fig. 2(a) ) clearly proves the presence of an ordered BCC (B2) phase.
Individual ionic/elemental reconstructions of Ni, Fe, Co and Al atoms (Fig. 2(c) ) reveal a homogenous elemental distribution.
Thus, these AlCoFeNi samples consist of a single phase with a B2 crystal structure.
The lowest microhardness value of 406 VHN was observed for the AlCoFeNi alloy annealed at 1000 °C
limitations: Finer scale second phase precipitates or phase separation may be present but not revealed at the coarse length scale of SEM imaging.

intervention.description: Annealing at elevated temperature for 15 hours

structure.description: Two-phase mixture of B2 matrix and fine scale Fe-Co rich BCC precipitates
microstructure: B2 matrix rich in Al and Ni

evidence_units.mechanism: Phase separation of the B2 matrix into Al-Ni rich B2 and Fe-Co rich BCC phases due to thermodynamic instability at lower temperatures, confirmed by superlattice spots in TEM and compositional partitioning in APT.
evidence_spans: The TEM results after annealing the AlCoFeNi alloy at 600 °C for 15 h are shown in Fig. 3 .
Similar to the previous condition, superlattice spots corresponding to the B2phase are evident.
Fine scale precipitate-like regions rich in Fe and Co were observed, the matrix is rich in Al and Ni.
From the APT and TEM results, the two phases can be characterized as the Al-Ni rich B2 matrix interspersed with fine scale precipitates of a Fe-Co rich BCC phase.
The APT results revealed that the average compositions of the BCC phase is 6Al-40Co-49Fe-5Ni (at%), while that of the B2 phase was determined to be 32Al-18Co-17Fe-33Ni (at%).

Interestingly, the 600 °C annealed condition of the AlCoFeNi alloy also exhibits a very high microhardness of 474 VHN, despite the fact that only an early stage of phase decomposition into B2 + BCC was exhibited by this sample.
limitations: The decomposition is described as an 'early stage' compared to the Cr-containing alloy.

evidence_spans: Co was partially replaced by Cr in the case of the AlCo0.5Cr0.5FeNi alloy to investigate the influence of Cr addition on the microstructure.
Both the heat treatment conditions resulted in the formation of a bright contrast faceted phase within a grey contrast matrix.
Note that the coarser precipitation of the bright phase is limited to the near-grain boundary region in the 600 °C sample ... while it extended throughout the grains in the 1000 °C condition.
Hence, addition of Cr to AlCoFeNi substantially changes the microstructure by introducing a strong tendency of phase separation in the B2 phase to form a two-phase mixture.
Apart from the intragranular precipitation/phase separation, there is clear evidence of a grain boundary phase forming in the case of the 1000 °C/15 h annealed sample, exhibiting a bright contrast
The coarse layer of the grain boundary phase was identified to be FCC in the case of the 1000 °C/15 h annealed sample
While intragranular decomposition is visible in this same sample, these regions were all indexed as a BCC phase in EBSD-OIM
The strong tendency of Cr to introduce phase separation in the B2 phase can possibly be attributed to a positive enthalpy of mixing of Fe-Cr, Co-Cr and Ni-Cr systems

intervention.description: Annealing at elevated temperature for 15 hours

structure.description: Hierarchical multi-scale B2 + BCC decomposition including BCC gen-1 (coarse), gen-2 (intermediate), and gen-3 (nano) precipitates
microstructure: Nano-scale precipitation in addition to coarser micron-scale decomposition
B2 matrix with cubical/spherical BCC precipitates
Fine scale Cr rich regions (gen-3) within B2 matrix
Coarse BCC lamellae along grain boundaries (gen-1)
Intermetallic sigma phase at grain boundaries

candidate.mechanism: Cr addition promotes strong phase separation into B2 + BCC; lower temperature (600 °C) refines the decomposition length scale to multiple generations (gen-1, gen-2, gen-3) due to kinetic constraints and thermodynamic driving force for Cr segregation.
limitations: Gen-1 BCC phase precipitates were not captured within the APT reconstructions as samples were prepared from grain interiors.
evidence_spans: The lowest microhardness value of 406 VHN was observed for the AlCoFeNi alloy annealed at 1000 °C, while the highest microhardness value of 475 VHN was observed in case of the AlCo 0.5 Cr 0.5 FeNi alloy annealed at 600 °C.

These observations can be qualitatively rationalized based on the fact that in case of the former, a single B2 phase is present in the 1000 °C annealed condition of the AlCoFeNi alloy, while in case of the latter a multi-scale hierarchical B2 + BCC decomposed microstructure was observed in case of the 600 °C annealed condition of the AlCo 0.5 Cr 0.5 FeNi alloy.
The 600 °C annealed sample (Fig. 4(d) ) shows nano-scale precipitation in addition to the coarser micron-scale decomposition seen in both 600 °C and 1000 °C annealed samples.

The APT reconstruction in Fig. 7(a) shows the Ni ions in blue and Cr ions in red. The large Cr rich BCC region on the left of the reconstruction is marked as BCC gen-2 BCC and the fine (nanometre) scale Cr rich regions are marked as BCC gen-3 regions.
The coarse micron-scale BCC lamellae, Figs 4(d) and 6(a) , are the generation-1 BCC phase, precipitated in the early stages and consequently grown to a larger extent.
The large Cr rich BCC region on the left of the reconstruction is marked as BCC gen-2 BCC and the fine (nanometre) scale Cr rich regions are marked as BCC gen-3 regions.

These nanometer scale precipitates are not visible in the TEM images shown in Fig. 6 , and are only visible in the APT reconstructions, revealing a new length scale of decomposition within this hierarchically decomposed microstructure.
